messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: 
- The failing test org.apache.commons.lang.StringEscapeUtilsTest.testEscapeJavaScript() first verifies that calling StringEscapeUtils.escapeJavaScript(null, null) and StringEscapeUtils.escapeJavaScript(null, "") throws IllegalArgumentException. This behavior matches the implementation: escapeJavaScript(Writer, String) delegates to escapeJavaStyleString(Writer, String, boolean), which immediately throws IllegalArgumentException when the Writer is null (lines 171–177).

- The core assertion expects that the input string
  document.getElementById("test").value = '<script>alert('aaa');</script>';
  is escaped to
  document.getElementById(\\\"test\\\").value = \\'<script>alert(\\'aaa\\');<\\/script>\\';
  Notably, this expects:
  - double quotes -> \"
  - single quotes -> \'
  - backslashes where needed
  - and crucially, the forward slash in </script> to be escaped as <\/script>.

- The implementation path for String escaping is:
  - StringEscapeUtils.escapeJavaScript(String) -> escapeJavaStyleString(str, true) (lines 121–123, 148–156).
  - The writer-based worker method escapeJavaStyleString(Writer, String, boolean) handles escaping of single quotes (when escapeSingleQuote is true), double quotes, backslashes, control chars, and unicode (lines 221–239). It does not include any case for the forward slash '/'.

- Because '/' is not escaped, the output will contain </script> instead of <\/script>, causing the assertion to fail.

- This aligns exactly with the current bug report: “StringEscapeUtils.escapeJavaScript() method did not escape '/' into '\/', it will make IE render page uncorrectly,” with the provided example expecting </script> to become <\/script>.

Conclusion: The failure is due to StringEscapeUtils.escapeJavaStyleString(Writer, String, boolean) not escaping the forward slash character. The JavaScript-specific escaping should add a case to emit '\/' for '/' so that escapeJavaScript(...) produces <\/script>, satisfying the test and preventing IE parsing issues described in the report.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
